newsitem.title: USA: Study finds education can cut student steroid use.
newsitem.headline: Study finds education can cut student steroid use.

text.p: Education programmes aimed at students and parents can help discourage high school atheletes from using body-building anabolic steroids, researchers said on Tuesday.
The finding from Oregon Health Sciences University in Portland was based on a study of 37 high school football teams in the Portland area, some of which were subjects of an educational effort.

Among students who took part in the study, there were "significant reductions in adolescent intent to use (steroids)" as well as higher self-esteem, better drug refusal skills and improved nutrition and exercise behaviour, the study said.
The students were given 14 educational sessions taught by coaches and student team leaders. Their parents were given one class.

Anabolic steroids are used by athletes to increase muscle growth, strength and performance. It has been estimated that by 1990 more than a quarter million high school students in the United States had used them.
Their adverse effects include a heightened risk of heart attack and abnormal liver function, as well as stunted height and severe mood and psychotic disorders.
